issues.legal_issue: The probate requirement for establishing testamentary rights does not unconstitutionally discriminate against Indian Christians when it also applies to other communities in historically defined circumstances.
material_facts: The petitioners challenged the requirement to obtain probate or letters of administration before establishing a right as executor or legatee under a will.
The requirement applied to Christians, but also applied to certain wills made by Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains, and to certain wills made by Parsis.
The scope of the requirement differed according to historically defined territories and the location of immovable property.
A state amendment had removed the requirement for Indian Christians in one state, while the petitioners pointed to differing treatment of property situated elsewhere.
issues.conclusion: The provision was not shown to discriminate against Christians as a separate class, because the probate requirement was not limited to Christians. The historical and geographical differences did not make the law unconstitutional, and the petitions were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 213(1) and 213(2) of the Indian Succession Act, read with Section 57(a), (b) and (c), apply the probate requirement to specified categories of wills and communities rather than exclusively to Christians. Historical reasons may justify differential treatment of geographical regions when the distinction bears a reasonable relation to the subject; variations between states in a federal system do not, by themselves, make the law discriminatory or invalid. The Court found it unnecessary to rely on the earlier decisions cited by the petitioners.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a rule requiring probate to establish testamentary rights.
predicates.probate_requirement_applies_to_multiple_: The requirement applied to Christians and also to members of other communities in specified circumstances.
predicates.classification_has_historical_geographic: The different application of the requirement reflected historically defined geographical categories.

issues.definition: When a validity challenge concerns a probate requirement that applies to multiple communities and rests on historically defined geographical distinctions, the requirement is not unconstitutional on the ground that it discriminates against one community.

issues.legal_issue: A person claiming as executor or legatee under a will cannot establish that right in court without probate or letters of administration when the will falls within a category subject to the requirement.
material_facts: One petitioner claimed to be the sole beneficiary under a will and sought to establish a right to property under it.
The petitioners argued that the probate requirement prevented a Christian legatee from establishing a right in court without first obtaining probate or letters of administration.
The statutory scheme applied the requirement to Christians and to specified wills of other communities, while exempting other categories of wills.
issues.conclusion: The bar concerns establishing a right as executor or legatee in a court of justice without the required grant. It does not prevent a will from being considered for other purposes, or prevent its reference in administrative or other tribunal proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Section 213(1) bars establishment in a court of a right as executor or legatee under a will without probate or letters of administration. Section 213(2), read with Section 57(a), (b) and (c), limits the categories to which that requirement applies. The bar concerns the asserted capacity of executor or legatee, whether the claimant appears as plaintiff or defendant, and does not prohibit consideration of the will for other purposes. The Court also referred to the application of the requirement to specified Parsi wills following the Indian Succession (Amendment) Act, 1962.

predicates.court_proceeding_to_establish_executor_o: A claimant seeks in court to establish a right under a will in the capacity of executor or legatee.
predicates.will_within_compulsory_probate_category: The will falls within a category for which a probate or equivalent grant is required before the testamentary right may be established in court.
predicates.probate_or_letters_not_granted: No probate or letters of administration for the will has been granted by a competent court.

issues.definition: If a claimant seeks in court to establish an executor's or legatee's right under a will within a compulsory-probate category and no required grant has been made, that right cannot be established in court.
